cues.en: (bright tones)
cues.zh: （輕快音調）

cues.en: Instructor: Hello, everyone and welcome to an Introduction to Linear Regression.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎來到線性迴歸簡介。

cues.en: In this lecture, we're going to give a light theoretical background and history behind the idea of linear regression before we actually tackle the concept with Python and the scikit-learn Library.
cues.zh: 實際用 Python 與 scikit-learn 前，先介紹線性迴歸的一點理論背景與歷史。

cues.en: If you want a deeper mathematical understanding of linear regression, you can go ahead and check out chapters two and three of an "Introduction to Statistical Learning."
cues.zh: 想深入數學，可以閱讀《Introduction to Statistical Learning》第二、三章。

cues.en: Let's discuss the history behind linear regression.
cues.zh: 談談線性迴歸歷史。

cues.en: This entire idea all started back in the 1800s with a man named Francis Galton.
cues.zh: 概念始於十九世紀的 Francis Galton。

cues.en: Galton was studying the relationship between parents and their children.
cues.zh: Galton 研究父母與子女的關係。

cues.en: And in particular, he investigated the relationship between the heights of fathers and the heights of their sons.
cues.zh: 尤其是父親與兒子的身高關係。

cues.en: What he discovered was that a man's son tended to be roughly as tall as his father.
cues.zh: 發現兒子的身高往往大致與父親相近。

cues.en: However, Galton's breakthrough was that the son's height tended to be closer to the overall average height of all people.
cues.zh: 但突破是，兒子的身高往往更接近所有人的整體平均身高。

cues.en: Let's go ahead and take an example of this.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: Shaquille O'Neal, who's a famous NBA player, is very tall.
cues.zh: 知名 NBA 球星 Shaquille O'Neal 非常高。

cues.en: He's 7ft 1in or 2.2 meters tall.
cues.zh: 身高 7 呎 1 吋，或 2.2 公尺。

cues.en: If Shaq, as he is known, has a son, chances are he'll be pretty tall too.
cues.zh: 大家叫他 Shaq，如果他有兒子，很可能也很高。

cues.en: However, Shaq is such an anomaly in height that there's also a very good chance that his son is not going to be as tall as Shaq,
cues.zh: 但 Shaq 的身高如此特殊，很可能兒子不會像他一樣高，

cues.en: and it turns out this is the case.
cues.zh: 實際也確實如此。

cues.en: Shaquille O'Neal's son is pretty tall.
cues.zh: 他的兒子很高。

cues.en: He's 6ft 7in, but he is not nearly as tall as his dad, who was 7ft 1.
cues.zh: 有 6 呎 7 吋，但遠不及 7 呎 1 吋的父親。

cues.en: Galton calls this phenomenon regression.
cues.zh: Galton 把這個現象叫 regression，迴歸。

cues.en: As in a father's son's height tends to regress or drift towards the mean or average height of everyone else.
cues.zh: 也就是兒子的身高往所有其他人的平均身高回歸或靠近。

cues.en: Let's go ahead and begin to plot out this sort of example.
cues.zh: 開始畫出這種例子。

cues.en: Let's calculate a regression with only two data points which is the simplest possible example.
cues.zh: 只用兩個資料點計算迴歸，是最簡單的例子。

cues.en: Here we have two data points at x equals two and y equals four is one data point and then X equals five and Y equals 10 is another data point.
cues.zh: 一個點是 x=2、y=4，另一個是 x=5、y=10。

cues.en: These two little black dots.
cues.zh: 就是這兩個小黑點。

cues.en: All we're trying to do when we calculate our regression line is draw a line that's as close to every dot as possible.
cues.zh: 算迴歸線時，想做的只是畫出盡可能靠近每個點的直線。

cues.en: For classic linear regression or the least squares method, you only measure the closeness in the up and down direction.
cues.zh: 傳統線性迴歸或最小平方法，只量上下方向的距離。

cues.en: Here we have a perfectly fitted line because we only had two points.
cues.zh: 這裡只有兩個點，所以直線完美擬合。

cues.en: Now, wouldn't it be great if we could apply this same concept to a graph with more than just two data points?
cues.zh: 如果能把概念套用到超過兩個點的圖，不是很棒嗎？

cues.en: By doing this, we could take multiple men and their sons' heights and do things like tell a man how tall we expect his son to be before he even has a son.
cues.zh: 這樣可以用多對父子身高，甚至在人還沒生兒子之前，就告訴他預期兒子多高。

cues.en: And this is the idea behind supervised learning.
cues.zh: 這就是監督式學習的概念。

cues.en: We're gonna have a bunch of labeled data points, create a model, in this case, a linear regression, and try to take unlabeled data
cues.zh: 有一堆標記好的資料點，建立模型，這裡是線性迴歸，再試著輸入未標記資料，

cues.en: such as a father's height and spit back out label data, our prediction of the son's height.
cues.zh: 例如父親身高，輸出標籤，也就是預測兒子身高。

cues.en: Our goal with linear regression is to minimize the vertical distance between all the data points in our line.
cues.zh: 線性迴歸目標，是最小化所有資料點與直線的垂直距離。

cues.en: So in determining the best line, we're attempting to minimize the distance between all the points and their distance to our line.
cues.zh: 決定最佳直線時，嘗試讓所有點到直線的距離最小。

cues.en: There are lots of actually different ways to minimize this, the sum of squared errors, sum of absolute errors, et cetera, but all of these methods have a general goal of minimizing the distance between your line
cues.zh: 有很多方法，例如誤差平方和、絕對誤差和等等，但共同目標都是讓直線

cues.en: and the rest of the data points.
cues.zh: 到其他資料點的距離最小。

cues.en: For example, one of these most popular methods that we just described is the least squares method.
cues.zh: 例如剛介紹最熱門方法之一，最小平方法。

cues.en: Here we have a couple of blue data points along an x and y axis, and we wanna fit a linear regression line.
cues.zh: 這裡 x、y 軸上有一些藍點，要擬合線性迴歸線。

cues.en: And the question is, how do we decide which line is the best fitting one?
cues.zh: 如何決定哪條線最合適？

cues.en: We can go ahead and use the least squares method which we discussed earlier.
cues.zh: 可以用剛才討論的最小平方法。

cues.en: This method is fitted by minimizing the sum of the squares of the residuals.
cues.zh: 它透過最小化殘差平方和擬合。

cues.en: The residuals for an observation is the difference between the observation, the y-value, and the fitted line.
cues.zh: 一筆觀測值的殘差，就是觀測值 y 與擬合線的差。

cues.en: In this image, the residuals are marked by the red line, the difference between the true data point in blue, and your fitted model line, the black diagonal line.
cues.zh: 圖中紅線表示殘差，也就是真實藍點與黑色斜線模型之間的差。

cues.en: All right, in the next lecture, we're going to use scikit-learn and Python to create a linear regression model.
cues.zh: 下一堂用 scikit-learn 與 Python 建立線性迴歸模型。

cues.en: Then you'll have your own portfolio project exercise, and afterwards, we'll go over the solutions to that project.
cues.zh: 接著有自己的作品集專案練習，再講解解答。

cues.en: Thanks everyone, and I'll see you in the next lecture.
cues.zh: 謝謝大家，下一堂見。
